did: Home now keeps a phone's pairing however many times the owner signs in elsewhere: the cap of 32 sessions ends browser sessions only, and phones have their own cap of 16, past which a new pairing is refused instead of a phone being forgotten. The owner can list their paired phones from a browser, with the day each paired, when it last renewed, and a name they typed for it, rename one, and sign one out; no token or hash is ever shown. Two written privacy rules were broken narrowly, with the coordinator's approval: a session row now says it is a phone's, and a phone keeps the day it paired; identity.md was rewritten to say so. Contract epoch 12.

calls.title: How many phones an account may keep
options: a separate cap of 16, refused past it
phones counted in the shared cap of 32
calls.why: The owner asked to keep phones past 32 but named no bound; uncapped breaks the bounded rows per account, and evicting a phone is the failure this removes.

calls.title: How long a phone's pairing lasts
calls.why: A phone's token sits in app storage, easier to lift than a cookie, and a phone in use renews itself when it opens.
calls.undo: Give phones their own term in pair_phone and the session slide.

calls.title: What "last seen" is
options: derived from when the session last renewed
a last-seen time written on every request
calls.why: The auth tables keep no timeline of use (identity.md invariant 10); the derived time is honest to about half a term.
calls.undo: Add a last_seen column written by session_subject.

calls.title: How precisely the pairing time is kept
calls.why: The phone's "since" needs only the day, and a day times no one's use.
calls.undo: Store seconds in a new column.

calls.title: Phones paired before this change
calls.why: Old rows can't tell a phone from a browser; a forced re-pair would sign out phones that work.

calls.title: How the owner tells phones apart
options: a random id, the day and the owner's own name
a random id and the day
calls.why: The owner asked to name each phone; the device model would say what device it is, which the privacy rules forbid.
calls.undo: Drop the label column and field.

calls.title: Signing one phone out
options: a route to sign one phone out
calls.why: Losing one phone shouldn't mean signing out everything.

calls.title: Where a phone's name is set
options: while pairing and from the list
calls.why: The owner types it while pairing and can fix it later; a phone's own token can't rename it.
calls.undo: Drop label from pairing/finish or the PATCH route.

left: A phone paired before this change is still unprotected until its next request; nothing can recognise it sooner.
Calls C491-C498 land in some-ui's docs/calls from the SIGNIN worker, not from this session.
The lan web's phone list and the phone's own pairing name are SIGNIN7 and the phone stories, not built here.
